spec.summary: Add a score ratchet: a frozen, atom-level baseline (eval/twin/baseline_scenarios.json) of per-storyline and per-ATT&CK-technique results. CI fails on any unwaived drop and on any unrecorded improvement. Dated, capped waivers are the only way to accept a drop. `ratchet.py refresh` is the only way to record an improvement. A PR-time guard blocks edits that lower the baseline without a waiver. A nightly Layer C trend file stays advisory. A weakened-rule mutation proof runs in-process on a temp rules dir and leaves the repo untouched. Finding from reading the code: today NOTHING pins any mutation score. layer_a.py/scenario_matrix.py gate only on baseline TPR==1.0 and their own controls, and no test references mutation_robustness (grep of test_*.py is empty). eval/twin/baseline.json is informational (`_baseline_delta` only prints a delta) and the quality canary floor is 0.5 against a measured 0.875. So per-storyline robustness (measured now: it_intrusion 13/19, infra_takeover 12/16, ai_to_ot 12/12 applicable of 20, Layer A 34/37) could fall without turning CI red.
spec.approach:
DESIGN IN SEVEN PARTS. All paths below were verified by reading the repo, or are exact new paths.

0. WHAT EXISTS TODAY (verified)
 - eval/twin/baseline.json is frozen "byte-identical forever" (seed 7, many nulls). report.py::_baseline_delta only REPORTS a delta and never fails.
 - report.py::main has a floor: tpr==1.0, fpr==0.0, alert_count>0, and the ticketed LOW alert must still exist.
 - layer_a.py::_selfcheck, scenario_matrix.py::_selfcheck and evasion_search.main gate only on baseline tpr==1.0, catalogue coverage, their own pos/neg controls, and measured==declared rule parameters.
 - tools/detection_quality_eval.py has FLOOR=0.5 and PER_RULE_FLOOR=0.0.
 - eval/oracle_consistency.py::_ACCEPTED is the only existing "dated waiver" pattern. It closes stale waivers and is currently empty.
 - Measured by me on 2026-10-02 (scenario_matrix.run_all(7), in-process, ~6m45s under load): ai_to_ot 12/12 applicable (8 N/A), it_intrusion 13/19 (0.6842), infra_takeover 12/16 (0.75), pooled 37/47. Baselines: it_intrusion membership_ok=False, 3 incidents; chain_fidelity 0.6/0.5/0.5, FCR 1.0, directional_discrimination 0.0 on all three.
 - Because full lanes take minutes, the ratchet CONSUMES the artifacts the gate already writes. It does not re-run them.

1. UNIT OF SCORE = ATOM (this is what makes the ratchet unmaskable)
 A flat map scope->value, with scope strings in a closed namespace.
 A rate-only floor lets one fixed variant mask one newly broken variant. It also lets coverage growth look like a drop. Atoms avoid both: a new failing variant is a NEW atom (recorded as a known gap, not a regression), and a previously passing variant that now fails is a drop even if the pooled rate rises.
 Atom families:
 - scn/<scenario>/base/<metric>: tpr(higher), alert_order_ok(higher, bool as 1/0), incident_membership_ok(higher), directional_discrimination(higher), mttd_seconds(lower), chain_fidelity and false_correlation_rate (PINNED: they measure entity sharing, not causal order, so any change forces a human refresh), incident_count and fired_alerts (pinned).
 - scn/<scenario>/mut/<axis>/<variant> = pass|fail|n/a, rank n/a<fail<pass. Scenarios are ai_to_ot, it_intrusion, infra_takeover, from scenario_registry.ALL. Rows come from scenario_matrix.run_scenario.
 - lane_a/mut/<axis>/<variant> = pass|fail|n/a: the 37-variant AI-to-OT catalogue from layer_a.run_matrix rows (34/37 today). lane_a/base/{tpr,chain_fidelity,false_correlation_rate}.
 - scn/<scenario>/evasion/<step>/<loss|stretch_pct|ip_k|account_k>: from evasion_search.search_scenario rows[].measured. Value is an int, or "immune" for None on ip_k/account_k/stretch. Direction higher, "immune" is infinity. Also .../agree (bool, higher).
 - tech/<fw>:<technique>/cell/<scenario>/<step>/base = detected|missed|gap (gap = oracle has no expected rule; rank gap<=missed<detected, and detected->gap is a drop so editing an oracle to dodge a failure is visible).
 - tech/<fw>:<technique>/cell/<scenario>/<step>/<axis>/<variant> = retained|lost|n/a. Retained iff the step is not in row.steps_lost and not in row.tactic_lost (both verified keys of layer_a._cmp rows). EXCLUDE the cell where variant==drop_<step> (that is the lane's negative control; the matrix already treats it as graceful), and prefix lane-A cells with lane_a/.
 - tech/<fw>:<technique>/rule/<rule_id>/{fires,near_miss_held,boundary_too_loose_n}: from eval/attack/out/fire_check.json entries (verified keys: id, framework, tactic, technique, fired, near_miss.fully_held, near_miss.too_loose).
 - twin/<metric> from eval/twin/report.latest.json: tpr, fpr, evidence_completeness, mttd_seconds, mtti, alert_reduction_ratio, severity_calibration_error, attribution_accuracy, plus negative_controls.<name>. EXCLUDE date, elapsed_seconds, incident_reconstruction_time_ms (wall-clock) and mutation_robustness (covered by lane_a).
 - corpus_b/<case_id>/{missed_n(lower),fired_n(pinned)}, corpus_b/cross_case_merge_clean (higher): from corpus.latest.json per_case and cross_case_merge_clean.
 - quality/macro_f1 and quality/<rule_id[:8]>/f1 (higher): computed in-process via tools/detection_quality_eval.py (load_engine_rules, entry_results, references, rule_metrics, macro_f1, the same calls nightly-eval.yml makes). This ratchets 0.875 where the floor is 0.5.
 Technique key: f"{framework or 'attack'}:{technique}" from each expected rule's mitre block (fire_check also defaults framework to attack). Rules without a technique become unmapped:<rule stem>. A step whose expected_rules lists several techniques credits each of them. Companion rules share their sibling's technique, so T1110, T1046, T1021, T1071.004 and T1485 stay one technique each.
 Per-technique roll-ups (detected k/n, retained r/t, lost_cells) are DERIVED and printed and written to the report. They are not ratchet atoms, because the atoms already imply them.

2. FILES AND MODULES
 - eval/twin/ratchet.py (stdlib only, so the PR guard job needs no pip). It holds the direction table DIRECTION_RULES (ordered list of regex -> higher|lower|pinned), rank(), compare(baseline, current, waivers, today, restrict=None), the waiver validator, refresh, guard and the trend functions. Unknown atom families default to pinned, and test_ratchet asserts every committed atom matches an EXPLICIT rule. CLI:
   * check [--advisory] [--scope PREFIX] [--report PATH]
   * refresh --reason TEXT [--init] [--retire PREFIX ...] [--scope PREFIX]
   * guard --base GITREF
   * explain ATOM
   * trend-append and trend-diff
 - eval/twin/ratchet_measure.py. It holds pure builders atoms_from_scenario_result, atoms_from_layer_a, atoms_from_evasion, atoms_from_twin, atoms_from_fire_check, atoms_from_corpus_b, atoms_from_quality and technique_cells(oracle, rows, rule_catalogue). It also has measure_artifacts() and measure_live(scenario, seed, only_variants=None). Both modes share the builders. It uses its own rule_catalogue() that reads contracts/rules/*.yml (same loop as report._rule_tactic).
 - eval/twin/fingerprint.py::system_fingerprint(). sha256 over a fixed, sorted file list: contracts/**/*.yml|json, non-test py under services/{shared,ws2-normalization,ws4-detection,ws8-correlation}, eval/twin/{scenario,scenarios_extra,scenario_registry,report,negative_controls,plc_sim,degradation}.py, eval/twin/oracle*.yaml, eval/adversarial/{mutate,mutate_generic,layer_a,scenario_matrix,evasion_search,corpus_b}.py. Over-inclusion is safe (it only forces a re-run).
 - Stamp the fingerprint, additive and deterministic, into: layer_a.run_matrix (matrix top level), scenario_matrix.run_all, evasion_search's written envelope, corpus_b.run_corpus, and report.run (report["report"]["system_fingerprint"]). Also add "tactic_covered_steps": base.get("tactic_covered_steps") to the baseline dict in layer_a.run_matrix and scenario_matrix.run_scenario (needed for the cell/base atoms; today the baseline dict drops it). check REFUSES any artifact that is missing or whose fingerprint differs from the current tree ("stale artifact: re-run <lane>"). Skipping silently is the rot pattern this repo keeps hunting.
 - eval/twin/baseline_scenarios.json. JSON, sorted keys, 2-space indent. Layout: {"_comment":[honesty header: how to refresh, direction rules, "never edit by hand; guard enforces"], "schema":"fengarde-scenario-ratchet-v1","seed":7,"basis":"harness-measured","fingerprint":{...informational},"atoms":{scope:value},"history":[{date,reason,added:[..],improved:[..],retired:[..],lowered:[..],fingerprint}]}. history is APPEND-ONLY (guard enforces prefix-equality against the base ref). Created once by `ratchet.py refresh --init --reason "initial freeze of measured state"` AFTER a full gate run. Committed numbers are whatever that run measured, never hand-typed. Roughly 450 atoms, ~30 KB.
 - eval/twin/ratchet_waivers.json: {"schema":"fengarde-ratchet-waivers-v1","waivers":[]}. Entry: {id, scope (exact atom, or a prefix ending "/*" confined to ONE scenario or ONE technique, never "*"), floor (the lowest tolerated value or status), opened, expires, owner, reason (>=20 chars), evidence (issue/PR/doc path)}. Rules: expires - opened <= 45 days; unique id; the waiver never raises the baseline; a waiver whose atom is NOT regressing is a STALE WAIVER and fails (same closure as oracle_consistency); below floor, or after expiry, fails. Time is read from env RATCHET_TODAY, else UTC today (tests inject it). This is the only wall-clock dependence in the lane, and it is intentional: an expired waiver must turn the gate red with no code change.
 - eval/trend_layer_c.jsonl: committed seed file with a `#` header (same reader convention as eval/trend.jsonl: skip `#` lines, append-only, never edit rows).

3. SEMANTICS OF check (strict by default; this is the ratchet)
 For every baseline atom compare rank(current) vs rank(baseline):
 - lower rank: REGRESSION. Fails unless an unexpired waiver covers it and current >= waiver floor, in which case it is reported WAIVED. The baseline keeps the old high-water value.
 - equal: OK.
 - higher rank: IMPROVED-UNRECORDED. Fails with "run: python eval/twin/ratchet.py refresh --reason ...". Rationale: without this, a later slide back to the old level passes (slack in the ratchet). `check --advisory` (nightly, local exploration) reports instead of failing.
 - atom present in the baseline, absent now (variant removed, became n/a, storyline or step deleted): REGRESSION (coverage shrink). Cleared only by `refresh --retire <prefix> --reason`, which writes a retired entry to history.
 - atom absent from the baseline, present now: NEW. Fails as unrecorded until refresh, but it is NOT a regression even if its value is "fail". Adding a storyline therefore never lowers a score; it adds known-gap atoms that a human records.
 - number->None is a regression (a null cannot launder a drop). None->number is an improvement. Floats are compared as the 4-dp producer-rounded values with 1e-9 epsilon.
 The output prints per-scenario k/n and per-technique "detected k/n, retained r/t, lost cells" tables next to the frozen values, so the per-technique score is visible on every run. Report written to eval/twin/ratchet_report.latest.json (deterministic: no clock, sorted keys; add to .gitignore beside eval/twin/report.latest.json). Exit 1 on any failure.
 refresh: re-reads artifacts (same freshness check); REFUSES (exit 1) if any unwaived regression exists; merges new[atom] = better-of(old, current), so a waived regression keeps its high-water mark; adds new atoms; updates improved ones; applies --retire; requires --reason; appends one history entry; prints the diff; idempotent (second run says nothing to refresh and writes nothing).
 Lowering a baseline on purpose (e.g. a grader becomes more honest) is NOT done by refresh. It needs a waiver, or a `lowered` history entry made with `refresh --lower ATOM=VALUE --reason ... --evidence ...`, which guard accepts only with a non-empty reason and evidence.

4. THE PR GUARD (stops "just edit the JSON")
 `ratchet.py guard --base <ref>` reads the base version via `git show <ref>:eval/twin/baseline_scenarios.json` (read-only) and compares it to HEAD. If the file is absent at base, it passes with a notice (initial introduction). Otherwise any atom whose rank is lower at HEAD must be covered by (a) an unexpired waiver present in HEAD ratchet_waivers.json that validates, or (b) a `lowered` or `retired` entry in HEAD history carrying a reason and evidence. It also fails if history at HEAD is not an append-only extension of history at base, if schema or seed changed, or if the file was deleted. Stdlib only.
 ci.yml: new job `ratchet-integrity` (if pull_request, or push to main using github.event.before; skip when before is all zeros). It runs actions/checkout with fetch-depth: 0 and actions/setup-python (reuse the SHAs already in the file), then `python eval/twin/ratchet.py guard --base origin/${{ github.base_ref }}` (push: `--base ${{ github.event.before }}`). No pip install.
 .github/CODEOWNERS (new; owner decision) lists eval/twin/baseline_scenarios.json, eval/twin/ratchet_waivers.json and eval/twin/ratchet.py so changes need maintainer review. Add a PR-template line: "baseline or waiver change: link the evidence".

5. WIRING
 run_all_tests.sh: insert AFTER the existing line `$PY eval/twin/test_phase3_5.py` (~line 515). By then every artifact the ratchet consumes exists: fire_check (line 446), layer_a (489), corpus_b (492), scenario_matrix (501), evasion_search (504), report.latest.json (509). Two blocks in the file's own style (echo "== ... =="; LAST_HEADER=...; $PY ... || { fail=1; FAILED=... }):
   `$PY eval/twin/ratchet.py check`   -- the score gate
   `$PY eval/twin/test_ratchet.py`    -- instrument acceptance + mutation proof
 tools/check_test_wiring.py will find test_ratchet.py because it matches `$PY <path>`.
 ci.yml: contract-tests already runs run_all_tests.sh, so both steps gate CI with no edit to that job. Add after it, with `if: always()`, a step uploading eval/twin/ratchet_report.latest.json via actions/upload-artifact at the SHA already pinned in the file (043fb46d..., v7.0.1), with if-no-files-found: warn. Add the `ratchet-integrity` job above. tools/verify_action_pins.py and actionlint cover the edits.
 Layer C trend, in nightly-adversary.yml (stays NON-BLOCKING; the 'Layer C never blocks' constraint holds, nothing here is added to the PR gate):
   * permissions add `actions: read`.
   * Step 1: restore the previous trend with the preinstalled gh CLI (no new action pin needed): `gh run list --workflow nightly-adversary.yml --status success --limit 1 --json databaseId -q .[0].databaseId` then `gh run download <id> -n layer-c-trend -D prev/ || true`. Copy prev/trend_layer_c.jsonl over the checked-out file if present. A first run or a >90-day gap just starts from the committed seed.
   * Then add `scenario_matrix.py --seed 7`, `evasion_search.py --seed 7` and `scenario_matrix.py --seeds 7,11,13,17` next to the existing layer_a.py step. The multi-seed run varies attack structure for the three storylines.
   * Run `adversary_c.py --seed 7 --llm`.
   * `ratchet.py check --advisory`.
   * `ratchet.py trend-append --layer-c eval/adversarial/out/adversary_c.latest.json` appends one row: {_schema:"layer-c-trend-v1", date, seed, producer (stub|llm), comparable (producer==stub), n_cases, n_pass, n_detection_lost, n_join_broken, cases:[{composition,pass,detection_retained,causal_join_broken}], ratchet_snapshot:{scenario_robustness, technique_retention, pooled, seed_spread:{scenario:{seed:robustness}}}, system_fingerprint}.
   * `ratchet.py trend-diff` writes $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and emits ::warning:: lines, ALWAYS exiting 0. It compares only comparable rows. For stub rows: same fingerprint and different result is flagged as a determinism BUG (::error:: annotation, still exit 0); different fingerprint is reported as "code changed". For llm rows it lists novel_evasions (compositions with detection lost that no earlier row recorded) as "promote to Layer A catalogue or Layer B corpus, then the ratchet locks it".
   * Upload artifact layer-c-trend (trend_layer_c.jsonl + ratchet_report) with retention-days: 90.
 The nightly workflow does not push, so a committed row comes from whoever runs trend-append locally (same convention as eval/trend.jsonl).
 nightly-eval.yml: add `python eval/adversarial/layer_a.py --seed 7` before the 'WP-1-F twin scorecard' step. The committed twin trend rows have mutation_robustness null because that lane never runs first.

6. MUTATION PROOF (inside eval/twin/test_ratchet.py; never leaves the repo weakened)
 I verified the mechanism by experiment on 2026-10-02 (scratch script, in-process, no repo write). Weakening BOTH dc_mass_vm_delete and dc_mass_vm_delete_by_source (siem.threshold 5 -> 7, the seed-7 mass_vm_delete burst size) in a temp rules dir and patching `report._WS4_MOD.RULES_DIR` (Detector reads that module global at construction, main.py:84) gave:
   STOCK:    baseline tpr 1.0; volume/thin_25pct pass=True.
   WEAKENED: baseline tpr STILL 1.0; thin_25pct pass=False, steps_lost=['mass_vm_delete'], tactic_lost=['mass_vm_delete'].
   RESTORED: pass=True again.
 So today's floors (tpr==1.0, matrix self-checks) stay green on this weakening, and only a per-variant ratchet sees it. Note that test_scenario_harness (i) hard-codes T=5 for this one rule, so it would catch this exact edit by luck; the ratchet is the general mechanism.
 Test steps:
   (1) hash every file in contracts/rules/ (S0).
   (2) Control: `measure_live('infra_takeover', 7, only_variants=[('volume','thin_25pct')])` compared with `restrict=` to that scenario and variant must be GREEN against the committed baseline. restrict skips derived/aggregate keys and anything not measured in the slice.
   (3) In `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()`, write the weakened copy of ALL rules (yaml.safe_dump, the same technique as test_layer_a._test_weakened_rule_drop). Set `report._WS4_MOD.RULES_DIR = tmp` inside try/finally and re-measure the same slice.
   (4) Assert compare is RED and names exactly: scn/infra_takeover/mut/volume/thin_25pct (pass->fail) and tech/attack:T1485/cell/infra_takeover/mass_vm_delete/volume/thin_25pct (retained->lost). Assert scn/infra_takeover/base/tpr is UNCHANGED at 1.0, which proves the old floors were blind.
   (5) Assert that a valid waiver for the first atom turns it WAIVED and the run green, and that the same waiver with an earlier `expires` turns it red. This closes the loop end to end.
   (6) finally: restore RULES_DIR. Assert `report._WS4_MOD.RULES_DIR is orig`, the rules hash equals S0, and a third measure is GREEN again.
 Cost: about 3 slice measures of 10-30 s each, ~1.5 min.
 The existing test_layer_a._test_weakened_rule_drop proves a single event stops firing. This new test proves the SCORE GATE goes red.

7. INITIAL BASELINE PROCEDURE (after implementation, one pass)
 Run the full gate (ratchet check will report 'no baseline'). Run `ratchet.py refresh --init --reason ...`. Review the diff by eye: the file will freeze known gaps (it_intrusion 6 failing variants, infra_takeover 4, Layer A 3 join-class rows, it_intrusion incident_membership_ok=False). Freezing means "do not get worse", NOT "accepted". The join-class rows need a change to the ratified WS-8 invariant, which is not touched. Then update the SSOT.md row with the measured atom count and per-scenario/per-technique numbers, marked PROVEN only after a green gate.
positive_and_negative_controls: POS: unchanged tree, fresh artifacts -> `ratchet.py check` exits 0 and prints WAIVED=0, REGRESSED=0, IMPROVED-UNRECORDED=0 (against the committed baseline).

NEG per family: take the committed baseline, doctor ONE atom downward in each family (scn base tpr, scn mut pass->fail, lane_a mut, evasion loss int, evasion ip_k immune->2, tech cell retained->lost, tech base detected->missed, fire_check fires, corpus_b missed_n, quality f1) -> check is RED and names that exact atom, with direction handled correctly for lower-is-better (mttd, missed_n).
NEG masking: baseline has variant A=fail, B=pass; current has A=pass, B=fail (pooled rate unchanged) -> RED on B. A rate-only floor would be green; this is the control that proves the atom design.
NEG null laundering: numeric atom -> None is RED; None -> number is IMPROVED-UNRECORDED.

NEG coverage shrink: delete a variant row, mark it n/a, or drop a whole scenario from current -> RED. POS: the same removal with `refresh --retire <prefix> --reason ...` passes and writes a history entry.

NEG improvement not silent: doctor one atom upward -> check RED with the refresh hint. POS: after `refresh --reason` the check is green, history has exactly one new entry, and a second refresh is a no-op (idempotent).

NEG refresh guard: with an unwaived regression present, `refresh` exits non-zero and writes nothing. POS: with a waived regression it records the improvements elsewhere while the waived atom keeps its high-water value.

WAIVER controls: valid unexpired waiver -> WAIVED and exit 0; current below waiver floor -> RED; expires < RATCHET_TODAY -> RED; window > 45 days -> RED; scope '*' or a prefix spanning two scenarios -> RED; waiver on a non-regressing atom -> STALE WAIVER RED; reason < 20 chars or missing evidence -> RED; duplicate id -> RED.

GUARD controls (synthetic base/head JSON through the pure function and one real temp git repo): lowered atom with no waiver and no lowered/retired entry -> RED; with an unexpired waiver -> GREEN; with a lowered entry carrying reason+evidence -> GREEN; history truncated or rewritten -> RED; file deleted or seed changed -> RED; file absent at base -> GREEN with notice.

FRESHNESS controls: an artifact whose system_fingerprint differs from fingerprint.system_fingerprint() -> RED 'stale artifact'; a missing artifact -> RED (never skipped); changing one byte of one contracts/rules file in a temp copy changes the fingerprint; two calls are equal.

TECHNIQUE mapping controls on a synthetic rule catalogue and oracle: steps with two expected rules credit both techniques; a no-rule step becomes a gap cell; the drop_<step> variant excluded for its own step (NEG: without the exclusion every technique shows a lost cell, test asserts the exclusion is what prevents it); a rule with no technique becomes unmapped:<stem>; companion shares the sibling technique.

DIRECTION table completeness: every atom in the committed baseline matches an explicit DIRECTION_RULES entry (none falls to the default 'pinned'); a synthetic atom in an unknown family is pinned (any change flags).
DETERMINISM: building the ratchet report twice from the same inputs gives byte-identical JSON (no clock in it); atom builders never read the wall clock; refresh output is sorted.

MUTATION PROOF (section 6): weakening the mass-VM-delete rules' threshold to the burst size in a temp rules dir turns the ratchet RED on the named variant and technique atoms while base tpr stays 1.0; the repo's rules hash and RULES_DIR identity are unchanged afterwards and the re-measure is GREEN again.

LAYER C trend controls: trend-diff on two synthetic comparable stub rows with equal fingerprints and different results emits a determinism ::error:: and still exits 0; an llm row is never compared with a baseline; trend-diff and trend-append never return non-zero on grade failures, so Layer C stays non-blocking; comment lines starting # are skipped when reading.
acceptance: `python eval/twin/ratchet.py check` exits 0 on the committed tree after a full run_all_tests.sh pass. It prints per-scenario k/n and a per-technique detected/retained table, each next to the frozen value.
`python eval/twin/test_ratchet.py` exits 0. It runs every control listed above, including the live weakened-rule proof, and `git status` shows no change to contracts/rules/ afterwards.
The new steps are in run_all_tests.sh; `python tools/check_test_wiring.py` still passes; `python tools/verify_action_pins.py` passes; ci.yml and the nightly workflows pass actionlint.

A deliberate, hand-made drop (e.g. flip one pass->fail in a copy of the artifacts, or the temp-dir rule weakening) makes the gate fail with the atom id; a hand-made improvement fails with the refresh instruction; neither is possible to land silently.

eval/twin/baseline_scenarios.json is produced only by `ratchet.py refresh --init`; its atom values equal the measured values (spot-check against matrix.latest.json, scenario_matrix.latest.json, evasion_search.latest.json); it contains no hand-typed number. eval/twin/baseline.json is byte-unchanged.
`ratchet.py guard --base origin/main` is green on the introducing PR (file absent at base) and red in a test PR that lowers an atom without a waiver or lowered-entry.
The nightly Layer C step appends a `layer-c-trend-v1` row, uploads `layer-c-trend`, and the job stays green even when Layer C cases fail or the ratchet reports a regression (advisory).

Honest status: SSOT.md row added only after the above are PROVEN. It states the baseline freezes known gaps (it_intrusion 13/19, infra_takeover 12/16, Layer A 34/37, WS-8 join-class rows) and does not claim that oracles are independent, that there are more than 3 storylines, or that chain_fidelity/FCR measure causal order.
risks: Wall-clock waiver expiry makes the gate time-dependent. Mitigation: RATCHET_TODAY override, the 45-day cap, and it is documented as intentional. Owner can switch expiry to warn-only locally.

Strict improvement-must-be-refreshed causes merge conflicts on baseline_scenarios.json when two PRs improve different atoms. Mitigation: atoms are sorted keys, one per line, so conflicts are line-local and refresh is idempotent (rerun after rebase). Alternative is warn-on-improve for PRs and strict on main.

Baseline freezes today's known failures, which a reader could mistake for acceptance. Mitigated by the _comment header, the SSOT wording, and per-atom 'fail' being visible in the report. Join-class rows still require the ratified WS-8 invariant change.

Stamping the fingerprint and adding tactic_covered_steps changes four lane outputs. tests that compare matrix dict shapes or key sets (test_layer_a, test_scenario_harness repr equality) may need updating; the stamp is deterministic so byte-determinism assertions hold.

Runtime: the ratchet check itself is seconds (artifact read), but the live mutation proof adds ~1.5 min to the gate, which already takes tens of minutes. The slice is deliberately limited to one scenario and one variant.

Namespace growth: every future instrument (steps 1-5, third-party corpus) must register an atom builder and a DIRECTION_RULES entry or the completeness test fails. That is intentional, but it is a tax on new work. Ratchet can land first against today's instruments and gain atoms as they land.

If the same atom is regressed by an intended improvement elsewhere (e.g. a companion rule changes which rule fires), the PR needs a waiver or lowered entry; reviewers need to read the history diff, not just CI.
gh run download chain depends on artifact retention (90 days) and `actions: read`; a gap restarts the trend from the committed seed. Not a correctness risk for the PR gate.

New actions/cache is deliberately NOT used because its SHA pin was not verified offline; if the owner prefers it, resolve the SHA with `gh api repos/actions/cache/git/ref/tags/<tag>` and let tools/verify_action_pins.py confirm.
needs_owner_decision: Strict vs warn: should an UNRECORDED improvement or new atom fail CI (recommended: yes, otherwise the ratchet has slack), or only warn on PRs and fail on main?

Waiver policy: 45-day cap, who may approve (propose CODEOWNERS on eval/twin/baseline_scenarios.json, eval/twin/ratchet_waivers.json and eval/twin/ratchet.py), and whether expiry is enforced by wall clock in CI (recommended) or only on main. Adding .github/CODEOWNERS only helps if branch protection requires code-owner review; per standing memory, it must never be bypassed with --admin.

Accepting the initial freeze: the baseline will record the known gaps as 'fail' atoms (it_intrusion 13/19, infra_takeover 12/16, Layer A 34/37, three WS-8 join-class rows, it_intrusion incident_membership_ok=False). Freezing them does not change them. Closing the join-class rows needs a change to the ratified WS-8 invariant (ADR-009/010 'tracks never merge'), which is the owner's call, not this step's; the ratchet works without it.

Whether chain_fidelity and false_correlation_rate stay in the baseline as 'pinned' (any change forces a human refresh) or are dropped from ratcheting entirely, given directional_discrimination=0.0 means they measure entity sharing and not causal order.
Whether Layer C 'llm' novel-evasion findings should auto-open issues (needs issues:write) or only appear in the job summary (default in this spec).
Persistence of the Layer C trend: artifact chain via gh run download (this spec) vs a scheduled commit-back job (contradicts the repo's 'do not auto-commit / contents: read' convention).
The mutation proof's weakening (mass-VM-delete threshold 5 -> burst size) is the one I verified. Confirm you are happy that the proof lives in the blocking gate (~1.5 min) rather than only nightly.

wrong_claims: Section 0 cites eval/oracle_consistency.py::_ACCEPTED. That path does not exist. The file is eval/twin/oracle_consistency.py, and _ACCEPTED is an empty dict at line 84, not a 'dated waiver' structure.

Mutation proof step (4) says the compare 'names exactly' scn/infra_takeover/mut/volume/thin_25pct and the T1485 cell. I measured the weakened tree (dc_mass_vm_delete and dc_mass_vm_delete_by_source threshold 5 -> 7, seed 7). Base fired_alerts drops 5 -> 3, so the pinned atom scn/infra_takeover/base/fired_alerts also changes. Base tpr, chain_fidelity, FCR, incident_count and mttd are unchanged. An exact-set assertion would fail on the author's own mechanism. The rest of the mechanism reproduced: stock thin_25pct passes, weakened gives pass=False with steps_lost=['mass_vm_delete'] and tactic_lost=['mass_vm_delete'], and restoring RULES_DIR passes again. Detector, negative_controls.Detector and report._WS4_MOD share one module globals dict, so patching RULES_DIR is valid.

The per-technique 'retained' cell (not in steps_lost and not in tactic_lost) is not per-technique. steps_lost means no alert at all at the step. tactic_lost (report._tactic_covered_steps) is satisfied by ANY rule with the same ATT&CK tactic. Weakening or losing the T1110 rule while T1110.004 password_spray still fires at that step counts as 'retained'. scenario_matrix already records the stricter expected_rule_lost_steps (_expected_lost), and the spec ignores it. The tech/.../base 'detected' value is likewise tactic-coverage, not the expected rule firing.

The 'check REFUSES any artifact whose system_fingerprint differs' claim does not cover all inputs. eval/attack/out/fire_check.json is a bare JSON list (34 dicts) and is not in the stamping list. Its rule/<id>/fires, near_miss_held and boundary_too_loose_n atoms can be read stale from a gitignored directory (eval/attack/out/ is in .gitignore). Quality atoms are computed in-process and are fine.

Section 1 puts twin/negative_controls.<name> under report.latest.json metrics. In the real file negative_controls is under context (metrics has no such key). The system_fingerprint stamp location report['report'] does exist.

'Roughly 450 atoms, ~30 KB' is an underestimate. Oracle steps are 7 + 6 + 3. Technique cells cover steps x variants per scenario (about 140 + 114 + 48) plus lane_a 7 x 37 = 259 (about 560 before multi-technique crediting). With 34 fire_check rules x 3, the other families, and steps crediting several techniques, the total is nearer 900-1100 atoms and ~70-100 KB.

'pinned' atoms (chain_fidelity, false_correlation_rate, incident_count, fired_alerts) have no defined rank order, but check and guard are specified only for lower/higher rank. A pinned change is neither a REGRESSION nor an IMPROVED-UNRECORDED. A real fidelity collapse (chain_fidelity 0.6 -> 0.1) can therefore be accepted by plain `refresh --reason`, and guard (which only looks at 'rank lower') will not catch it.

The nightly step `gh run list` / `gh run download` omits `env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`. The preinstalled gh CLI fails unauthenticated, and the spec's `|| true` then silently restarts the trend from the seed on every run. The failure is invisible, the same rot pattern the repo keeps hunting.
missing: Sub-criterion masking: the mut atom is only `pass`, a conjunction of detection_retained, fidelity_retained, fcr_unchanged, order_retained and decoy_clean. A variant already `fail` (it_intrusion has 6, infra_takeover 4, Layer A 3) can lose order, gain decoy contamination or break fidelity further and stay `fail`, so the ratchet does not move. Only the detection part is partly covered by the tech cells. Record each sub-criterion (row keys exist in both matrices) as its own atom, plus expected_rule_lost_steps and causal_join_broken.

History merge conflicts are certain, not just possible. Every PR that runs refresh appends to the same tail of the `history` array in one JSON file, so any two concurrent refreshing PRs conflict textually. Sorted atom keys do not help. Move history to an append-only eval/twin/ratchet_history.jsonl with .gitattributes `merge=union`, or key entries by date and id.

The `refresh --lower ATOM=VALUE --reason --evidence` path that guard accepts has no expiry, no cap and no content check beyond 'non-empty'. It is a permanent unwaived lowering, weaker than the 45-day waiver. Require the same quality bar as a waiver (>=20 chars, evidence must be a PR or issue URL or an existing doc path) or drop it. The guard also lets the same PR add the waiver or history entry that excuses its own drop. That is only controlled by CODEOWNERS plus branch protection.

Solo-maintainer deadlock: CODEOWNERS only works if branch protection requires code-owner review, and GitHub does not let an author approve their own PR. With one owner every baseline-touching PR would need `--admin`, which the memory rule forbids. Put this in needs_owner_decision, and consider making `ratchet-integrity` a required status check instead.

The ratchet-integrity job is only a gate if it is a required status check. It does not run in run_all_tests.sh, so a local or `make test` user can hand-edit a baseline downward and `check` passes (current >= edited baseline). Add a cheap local equivalent (guard against `git merge-base HEAD main` when available) or document that this is CI-only.

The mutation proof's control (2) compares a live stock slice against the COMMITTED baseline. If a legitimate waived or lowered baseline ever touches thin_25pct, the proof breaks for the wrong reason. It is also unusable before the first `refresh --init`, and that init is specified to happen after a gate run that already contains test_ratchet. Make the proof hermetic: build the baseline from the stock slice in-process, then compare the weakened slice.

Cross-platform determinism is unproven: the baseline is generated on Windows and gated on ubuntu CI (glob order, set iteration, float rounding in 4-dp producer values). Either generate the initial baseline from a CI Linux artifact, or add a one-time CI run that proves `check` is green on Linux before the PR is merged.

Dependency on the dirty tree: the initial freeze must come from a committed state. contracts/rules/*_by_*.yml, the companion rules and the harness edits are currently untracked or modified, and the fingerprint covers them. The ratchet PR must land after, or together with, that tree being committed.

ratchet.py must import yaml/ratchet_measure lazily. The stdlib-only `guard` job installs no pip packages, but check/refresh need PyYAML (rule_catalogue and oracle loading). ci.yml's contract-tests job already installs pyyaml, so check is fine there.

tools/check_test_wiring.py and the dormant-test guard (commit a9b9313) require test_ratchet.py's test functions to actually be called from its main. Also state that the new `ratchet.py check` line is not a test_*.py, so wiring is only enforced by review.

Strict 'new atom fails until refresh' means any new rule, variant or oracle step (even a pure addition) turns CI red until a baseline refresh. The spec treats this as intended but does not size it: the PR template should include the refresh command, and the owner decision on strict vs warn is load-bearing.
